topic: GST Council and 101st Amendment — mixed tiers
description: Article 279A, composition, voting, slabs, recent decisions, exam-favourite niche details

questions.stem: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the:
questions.explanation: 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 — added Article 246A (concurrent powers to Centre and States to levy GST), Article 269A (IGST), Article 279A (GST Council). GST itself rolled out from 1 July 2017 (midnight session of Parliament). Subsumed multiple central + state taxes — Central Excise (except on tobacco, petroleum), Service Tax, Additional Customs Duty (CVD/SAD), Central Sales Tax, VAT, Entry Tax, Luxury Tax, Octroi, Entertainment Tax (except by local bodies). One-Nation-One-Tax. Petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas, crude — temporarily kept OUT of GST (still under VAT + excise); Council can include them later. 100th Amendment — was about land boundary agreement with Bangladesh.

questions.stem: The GST Council is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 279A — added by 101st CAA, 2016. The President to constitute the GST Council within 60 days of commencement of the amendment (constituted 12 Sep 2016). Composition: (1) Union Finance Minister — Chairperson; (2) Union MoS Finance (Revenue) — Member; (3) Finance Minister of each State — Member. The Vice-Chairperson is chosen from among the State Finance Ministers. Article 279 — Calculation of net proceeds, basis of devolution. Article 280 — Finance Commission (every 5 years). Article 312 — All-India Services.

questions.stem: What is the voting weightage of the Centre and the States in the GST Council?

options.option_text: Centre 1/3 (33.33%), States 2/3 combined; decisions need 75% of weighted votes (i.e., 3/4 majority)

questions.explanation: GST Council voting (Art 279A(9)): Centre's vote = 1/3 weight; all states combined = 2/3. Any decision requires 3/4 (75%) of weighted votes. So neither side alone can push a decision through — Centre alone has 33% (less than 75%), states alone have 67% (also less than 75%). Encourages cooperative federalism. Quorum = 50% of total membership. Each state gets equal weight regardless of size (small states equal to UP/Maharashtra). UTs with legislatures (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K post-2019) are also members. Note — May 2022 SC ruling (Mohit Minerals case) clarified that GST Council recommendations are NOT binding on Centre or States — only persuasive; Centre and States retain legislative competence.

questions.stem: Which of the following items is NOT currently under GST (kept outside the GST framework)?

options.option_text: Petroleum products (crude, petrol, diesel, ATF) and natural gas

questions.explanation: Items kept OUTSIDE GST (still taxed under earlier regime): (1) Petroleum products — crude oil, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas (under Central Excise + State VAT — that's why fuel prices vary state-to-state); (2) Alcohol for human consumption — exclusively State VAT (a key state revenue protected by constitutional carve-out); (3) Electricity — under Electricity (Tax on Consumption or Sale) by states; (4) Tobacco products (Central Excise levied IN ADDITION to GST). Real estate transactions — partially (under-construction property has GST 5%/12%, but completed property + land have stamp duty under state). Council can decide to bring petroleum under GST anytime, but states have resisted (collectively ~₹3-4 lakh cr revenue at stake).

questions.stem: The standard GST tax slab structure has FOUR main rates:

options.option_text: 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% (+ exempt 0% and a few special rates)

questions.explanation: Main GST rates: 0% (essentials — fresh food, milk, education, healthcare); 5% (mass-consumption — packaged food, transport, footwear ≤ ₹1000); 12% (semi-essentials — butter, ghee, mobile phones); 18% (most goods + services — soaps, computers, IT services); 28% (luxury + sin — air-conditioners, large TVs, automobiles, tobacco — plus a 'compensation cess' on top of 28% for tobacco, pan masala, automobiles, aerated drinks). Special low rates: 0.25% (rough diamonds), 3% (gold + jewellery). Compensation cess proceeds funded the GST Compensation Cess Fund — used to compensate states for revenue loss in the first 5 years of GST (later extended to repay COVID-period borrowings). Rate rationalisation has been an ongoing GoM agenda — the 'Group of Ministers' headed by various state FMs.

questions.stem: When a sale of goods happens FROM Maharashtra TO Karnataka (inter-state), the tax levied is:

options.option_text: IGST (Integrated GST) — collected by the Centre, then revenue split between Centre and the destination state (Karnataka)

questions.explanation: GST flow: INTRA-state (within same state) — CGST (Centre's share) + SGST (state's share), each 1/2 of the GST rate. Example: 18% intra-state → 9% CGST + 9% SGST. INTER-state — IGST collected by Centre at the FULL rate (= CGST + SGST equivalent); Centre then transfers the SGST-equivalent share to the DESTINATION state (consumption-based tax). UNION TERRITORY — UTGST instead of SGST (for UTs without legislatures). GST is a destination-based consumption tax — revenue accrues to the state where the goods/services are consumed, not where produced. This is a fundamental shift from the earlier origin-based central sales tax (CST), which had favoured producing states. Article 269A — IGST.

questions.stem: Who is the EX-OFFICIO chairperson of the GST Council?
questions.explanation: Union Finance Minister — ex-officio Chairperson of the GST Council (Article 279A(2)). Currently — Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman (since 2019). Members: Union MoS for Finance (Revenue) + each State Finance Minister (or other Minister nominated by the State). Vice-Chairperson — chosen from State FMs by them. Secretary to the Council — the Revenue Secretary (Govt of India). Council secretariat at New Delhi. Has met 50+ times since constitution. Decisions historically have largely been by consensus despite the 75% formal voting rule.
